note: The exact MCP tool calls behind the generated files in this directory. Both servers are the hosted OpenZeppelin endpoints; the Solidity in rwa-token.sol and hook-scaffold.sol is their verbatim output, unedited.

token.prompt: Generate a permissioned RWA token called APACPrivateCredit, symbol APCX. Transfers have to be restricted to an allowlist. I need to freeze an individual holder's balance, mint, burn, and pause the whole asset. Use role-based access control rather than a single owner, include ERC-2612 permit, and pre-mint 1,000,000 to the deployer. MIT licence, security contact security@openzeppelin.com.

hook.prompt: Scaffold a Uniswap v4 hook called CompliantSwapHook on top of BaseHook. It has to gate pool initialisation, gate liquidity adds, gate swaps, and observe swaps after they settle — so beforeInitialize, beforeAddLiquidity, beforeSwap and afterSwap, and nothing else.

rule.note: Not an MCP call. The compliance rule is the part no generator can produce, because it encodes a specific issuer's policy. These are the prompts that turned the scaffold above into the deployed contracts, written against the ERC-3643 call surface in contracts/interfaces/IERC3643.sol.

prompts.label: The decision function
prompts.text: Write the contract that answers Uniswap's question — what may this account do with this asset? — by reading the issuer's ERC-3643 registry rather than a venue-held list. Return PermissionFlags. Check in ascending cost: is the token paused, is the wallet frozen, is the identity verified, and only then the optional jurisdiction overlay. Grant LIQUIDITY_ALLOWED only when the account holds the configured professional-investor claim topic. Keep every external call in a try/catch so a malformed registry cannot brick the pool.

prompts.label: The enforcement bodies
prompts.text: Fill in the TODO bodies in the scaffold. beforeSwap requires SWAP_ALLOWED on both sides of the pair and swapping enabled on the adapter; beforeAddLiquidity requires LIQUIDITY_ALLOWED on both sides. Resolve the real initiating wallet through IMsgSender on the calling periphery contract, not msg.sender, so a custodian trading for a client is evaluated as the client. Revert with typed custom errors that name the account, the adapter and the flag that was missing. Skip enforcement entirely for any currency that is not a verified permissions adapter.

prompts.label: The adversarial tests
prompts.text: Write Foundry tests that try to break each control rather than confirm it. Prove an unverified wallet cannot reach the asset by any route, that a KYC-only investor can swap but reverts on liquidity provision, that freezing one custody client leaves its siblings trading, and that a jurisdiction block at the venue stops one country without touching another. Assert on the specific custom error, not just that the call reverted.
